scope: gold-bearing material identification, segregation, valuation, and professional refinery routing

workflow.title: Identify source
workflow.instruction: Record whether suspected gold-bearing material comes from connectors, fingers, processors, pins, plated hardware, jewelry, or another source.

workflow.title: Do not grade by color
workflow.instruction: Gold-colored material is not proof of gold content. Preserve source, markings, and Board Sense evidence until testing or buyer/refinery grading confirms value.

workflow.title: Keep categories separate
workflow.instruction: Separate gold fingers, processors, connector pins, plated hardware, jewelry-grade material, and unknown lots rather than mixing unlike feedstock.

workflow.title: Record weight and condition
workflow.instruction: Weigh clean lots and document contamination, base material, plating condition, and known grade information.

workflow.title: Compare intact and recovered value
workflow.instruction: Check specialty e-scrap, collectible/resale, and professional refinery paths before destructive processing.

workflow.title: Route for testing/refining
workflow.instruction: Use appropriate professional assay/refinery services when actual precious-metal content determines payout.

workflow.title: Time-value check
workflow.instruction: Compare sorting or safe mechanical preparation labor against the expected increase in buyer/refinery value.

hazard_policy: Gold chemical recovery can involve corrosive reagents, toxic gases, and hazardous waste. This lab provides identification, sorting, valuation, and professional refinery-routing guidance rather than uncontrolled chemical recipes.
